facts.statement: The name Moanasaurus means "Sea Lizard", derived from the Māori word for sea and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: Moanasaurus (From Māori moana "sea" and Greek sauros "lizard"; meaning "Sea Lizard")

facts.statement: With a skull measuring 78 cm in length, Moanasaurus was one of the largest members of the Mosasaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: The skull measures 78 cm in length, which shows that Moanasaurus was one of the largest in the subfamily of Mosasaurinae.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Moanasaurus have been discovered in the North Island of New Zealand.
facts.quote: Its fossil remains have been discovered in the North Island of New Zealand.

facts.statement: Moanasaurus is classified within the superfamily Mosasauroidea, family Mosasauridae, and subfamily Mosasaurinae.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Mosasauroidea familia: Mosasauridae subfamilia: Mosasaurinae

facts.statement: Moanasaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 to 66 million years ago, in the areas of modern-day Japan and New Zealand.
facts.quote: Moanasaurus es un género extinto de saurópsidos mosasáuridos que vivió durante el Maastrichtiense en el período Cretácico (era Mesozoica), hace entre 70-66 millones de años en el área de las actuales Japón y Nueva Zelanda.

facts.statement: The time range for Moanasaurus spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: A PhD thesis argued that Mosasaurus flemingi is a junior synonym of Moanasaurus mangahouangae.
facts.quote: The same thesis argued that Mosasaurus flemingi is a junior synonym of Moanasaurus mangahouangae.

rejected.quote: Moanasaurus was a very large mosasaurine known originally from holotype CD43, a disarticulated skull, vertebrae, ribs and flipper bones.
